Fit a Bayesian population pharmacokinetic model

Source: R/fit.R
bpk_fit.Rd

Samples the posterior with Stan (NUTS) using a precompiled closed-form model. The data are a NONMEM-style data frame used as is.

Usage

bpk_fit(
  model,
  data,
  priors = NULL,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = floor(iter/2),
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 1L),
  seed = sample.int(.Machine$integer.max, 1),
  adapt_delta = 0.9,
  prior_only = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

A model from pk_model().

data

NONMEM-style data frame.

priors

Priors from pk_priors(); unspecified ones get defaults.

chains, iter, warmup, cores, seed

Passed to rstan::sampling().

adapt_delta

Target acceptance rate of NUTS.

prior_only

Logical; sample from the prior only (ignores DV).

...

Further arguments to rstan::sampling().

Value

An object of class bpk_fit.

Details

Data columns (case-insensitive): ID, TIME, DV, AMT (required); EVID, MDV, RATE, ADDL, II (optional) and any covariates used in the model. "." is read as missing. Doses are records with EVID == 1 (or AMT > 0 when EVID is absent); observations are records with EVID == 0, MDV != 1 and a non-missing DV. Observations at or before the first dose of a subject are dropped with a message. Not supported in this version: steady-state records, reset events, modelled rates, time-varying covariates and below-quantification records.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("nlmixr2data", quietly = TRUE)) {
d <- nlmixr2data::theo_sd
mod <- pk_model("1cmt", route = "oral", iiv = c("CL", "V", "KA"))
fit <- bpk_fit(mod, d, chains = 2, iter = 1000, seed = 1)
summary(fit)
}
